title: Debug: One-Hot FSM
constraints: Intended behavior: a one-hot FSM, `state` = {FLUSH, RUN, LOAD, IDLE} (IDLE = bit 0). Exactly one bit may be set at any time.
IDLE → LOAD when `go`. LOAD → RUN (always). RUN → FLUSH when `done`, otherwise stays in RUN. FLUSH → IDLE (always).
`busy = !IDLE`. Synchronous reset → IDLE (`state = 4'b0001`). The starter has **2 bugs**.
hints: What does `state` look like right after reset? Is exactly one bit set?
Run the FSM into RUN and assert `done`. Print `state` for the next few cycles.
Each next-state bit of a one-hot FSM is an OR over its incoming transitions. Check the RUN self-loop condition.

examples.title: one job
examples.input: go, then done after 3 cycles of RUN
examples.expected: LOAD → RUN ×3 → FLUSH → IDLE, always exactly one hot bit
